correctness.rationale: For a height-one Gorenstein cone a crepant smooth toric projective resolution over the affine base corresponds precisely to a coherent unimodular triangulation, with marked morphism and no identification under symmetries. Verify the seven lattice points, primitive boundary and normalized polygon area seven, hence every resolution uses seven area-one triangles. Enumerate all 17 determinant-one triangles on those points and all compatible seven-triangle selections, exactly ten; exact area and incidence confirm no gaps or overlaps. Reconstructed all ten integer height assignments independently by exact affine interpolation: each of eight internal edge inequalities is strictly positive, proving every triangulation coherent. Full flips of empty unimodular quadrilaterals produce an independently enumerated connected 10-vertex/13-edge graph with stated degrees, BFS distances and unique distance-five pair. The finite enumeration is exhaustive over possible marked toric resolutions only, not non-toric/global resolutions.

final_claim: For the seven-lattice-point pentagon Q=conv{(0,0),(-2,-1),(-3,-2),(-2,-3),(-1,-2)} in Wuebben’s local singularity, there are exactly ten smooth toric crepant resolutions projective over the fixed cone, because all ten unimodular triangulations are regular. Their elementary toric flop graph has 13 edges, degree profile (1,3,5,1) for degrees 1..4, radius 3, diameter 5 and a unique antipodal pair.
